Tested on Windows 10, unable to reproduce:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6ca5b27-3d71-4330-8652-cfa65d7de7cb)

I can also reproduce this on my system both on 4.4.1 and 4.5 dev 1, using OP's MRP and a separate test project rendering just icon.svg on a 2D canvas.

For me, it happens in both Firefox and Chrome (slightly different error messages, but the project fails to launch in both). I'm using Aurora (based on Fedora Kinoite 41), running all three apps in Flatpak (I don't have access to a non-flatpak browser on this system), if that matters. The system I tested this on is a laptop with a Ryzen 5 7640U.

The issue persists even after clearing out the .godot directory in the project, so it's not a one-off import issue.

I've also seen two people on the Godot Cafe Discord with the same issue, though I haven't asked them about their system specs.

Note: Running the project natively (non-web export) causes no issues. 4.3 also works correctly, in web and native exports. Likewise, VRAM compressed textures works fine in all versions in web exports.

bump, same issue after upgrading to 4.4.1, basis universal textures prevent web build to work. 

Windows 11
Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700K CPU @ 3.80GHz, 3701 Mhz, 8 Core(s), 16 Logical Processor(s)
Update: This can only be reproduced with the official templates

Here's how official templates are built, with Emscripten 3.1.64: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-build-scripts/blob/main/build-web/build.sh

Most relevant flag would be `production=yes` which enables LTO.
Not sure where to look. The description sounds like a compiler error.
@adamscott have you run into any such issues before, or have any idea of where someone might be able to poke around to find the cause of this?
@michaelharmonart Could you check whether 4.4-dev3 loads correctly? If so, could you verify if 4.4-dev4 also works?

tested 4.4dev4 and had no issues so I continued by testing each dev and beta version version up till 4.4 beta 1 which was the first version to error out with the "indirect call to null"

something between 4.4 dev 7 and 4.4 beta 1 broke I guess

Do you think it'll help to ask for basisu upstream to debug web?

This issue also occurs when I call `texture.create_placeholder`
```gdscript
extends Sprite2D

func _ready() -> void:
	texture=NoiseTexture2D.new()
	texture.create_placeholder() # <--
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56f8c43f-5963-4077-a459-78208d998ba8)

Sounds like those signature mismatch are real bugs we should fix.

If we can't, we can go back to `lto=full` but this made linking take hours (in total) for web builds.

The issues we have seem to be the same as https://github.com/emscripten-core/emscripten/issues/10831.

The TL;DR is that `-flto=thin` can't be trusted for Emscripten, so we should go back to `-flto` (full LTO) :(

This issue looks very similar to what I encountered in a different project. I have a proposed fix at https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/136197. Can someone confirm if it solves your issue too?
